facts.fact: Scientists have discovered a Jupiter-like planet named HAT-P-7b where it rains rubies and sapphires. It is located 1000 light-years from Earth.
A single day on Venus takes 243 Earth days to complete, which is longer than its entire year of 225 Earth days.
The Sun makes up 99.86% of the mass of our solar system, and its core temperature reaches around 15 million °C.
The Andromeda Galaxy contains over a trillion stars and is on a collision course with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.
A supernova is a massive stellar explosion that can outshine entire galaxies for weeks.
Black holes are regions with gravity so strong that not even light can escape. Supermassive black holes can be billions of times the Sun's mass.
Quasars are extremely luminous active galactic nuclei powered by supermassive black holes.
Neutron stars are incredibly dense remnants of supernovae. A teaspoon of neutron star matter weighs about a billion tons.
A kilonova occurs when two neutron stars collide, producing heavy elements like gold and platinum and emitting gravitational waves.
Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are brief but extremely energetic flashes from stellar explosions or neutron star mergers.
Jupiter is so massive it could fit all other planets inside it. Its moon Europa may have a subsurface ocean.
Saturn’s rings span hundreds of thousands of kilometers but are only about 10 meters thick in some parts.
Our Milky Way galaxy contains around 100–400 billion stars. The solar system orbits its center at roughly 828,000 km/h.
Nebulae are clouds of gas and dust where new stars are born, like the Orion Nebula.
Pluto is a dwarf planet with a heart-shaped glacier region called Sputnik Planitia.
The first-ever image of a black hole, captured in 2019, showed the event horizon of the black hole in galaxy M87.
Exoplanets orbit stars beyond our solar system. Some are rocky and within the habitable zone.
Auroras occur when charged particles from the Sun interact with Earth's magnetic field, creating spectacular lights near the poles.
